title: Psalm 92: A Song for the Sabbath
summary: A song for the Sabbath declares that it is good to praise the LORD morning and night, with harp and lyre, for the greatness of his works and the depth of his thoughts. The wicked may sprout like grass, but they will perish, while the LORD is exalted forever. The righteous, planted in God's house, flourish like the palm and the cedar and still bear fruit in old age, proclaiming that the LORD is upright.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 92

line: A song for the Sabbath: it is good to praise the LORD morning and night, and the righteous, planted in God's house, still bear fruit in old age.
guide: Rest is not only stopping work; it is gladness at what God has done. Let verse 14 encourage anyone growing old: people rooted in God still bear fruit in prayer, wisdom and kindness.

stanzas.title: It is good to praise the LORD morning and night
God's deep thoughts and the wicked who sprout like grass
The righteous flourishing in God's house

verses.t: A Psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It is good to praise the LORD, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High,
to proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning and Your faithfulness at night
with the ten-stringed harp and the melody of the lyre.
For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds; I sing for joy at the works of Your hands.
How great are Your works, O LORD, how deep are Your thoughts!
A senseless man does not know, and a fool does not understand,
that though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they will be forever destroyed.
But You, O LORD, are exalted forever!
For surely Your enemies, O LORD, surely Your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
But You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; with fine oil I have been anointed.
My eyes see the downfall of my enemies; my ears hear the wailing of my wicked foes.
The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain,
to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.”
